subject: SLA amendment: assured uptime % and monthly remedy allocation — Aquila Health
messages:
From: Claire Dawson <claire@aquila-health.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: SLA uplift request and monthly credit cap

Markus —

Thanks for the demo last week. Aquila's legal and ops teams finished their initial review of the standard Redwood SLA and we need to surface two items before we can move to signature:

1) Uptime baseline: Our compliance team is pushing for a 99.99% monthly availability commitment (current template lists 99.95%). Given the criticality of the patient-facing inference pipeline, that extra decimal materially reduces our risk profile.

2) Monthly remedy cap: We need a hard cap on monthly service credits so our finance team can forecast liability. Ideally something like a maximum credit equal to the monthly subscription charge (1x monthly fee).

We also want clarity on scheduled maintenance carveouts — can you confirm maximum permitted maintenance per month and notification windows?

Attached is a short checklist from our procurement team (not a redline yet). Happy to set a call early next week to run through specifics.

Best —
Claire Dawson
Head of Procurement, Aquila Health
(attachment: aquila_procurement_checklist.pdf)
From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Claire Dawson <claire@aquila-health.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA uplift request and monthly credit cap

On Mon, Mar 1, 2027 at 9:12 AM Claire Dawson <claire@aquila-health.com> wrote:
> Markus —
>
> Thanks for the demo last week...

Hi Claire — thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the checklist. Quick answer up front: we can be flexible, but there are trade-offs between guaranteed uptime, maintenance carveouts, and the monthly liability cap. I outlined options below to make the trade-offs explicit.

Option A (standard, fast-path):
- Availability: 99.95% monthly
- Remedy: credits as % of monthly invoice (see matrix below)
- Monthly cap: 100% of monthly invoice (we can agree this)
- Maintenance carveout: up to 8 hours/month with 72h notice for non-emergency rolling upgrades.

Option B (higher SLA, committed capacity):
- Availability: 99.97% monthly (midpoint)
- Remedy: higher credit multipliers when breached (see matrix)
- Monthly cap: 150% of monthly invoice
- Maintenance carveout: 6 hours/month, 7 days notice

Option C (enterprise uplift — reserved capacity + tighter ops):
- Availability: 99.99% monthly
- Remedy: steeper credit scale, plus dedicated on-call and quarterly operational reviews
- Monthly cap: 200% of monthly invoice or negotiable via reserved capacity contract
- Maintenance carveout: negotiated, typically <4 hours/month

Sample remedy matrix (illustrative):
- >= 99.95% — no credit
- 99.90% to <99.95% — 10% credit of monthly invoice
- 99.00% to <99.90% — 30% credit
- <99.00% — 100% credit

If you need 99.99% without reserved capacity, we can propose Option C but that will have a material cost uplift (committed GPUs / SLAs). If your compliance team can accept 99.97% for the pilot, that often hits the sweet spot operationally.

I attached a clean copy of our SLA draft for reference (SLA_Draft_Aquila_v3.pdf). Happy to jump on a call with legal/ops to walk through the matrix and cap mechanics.

— Markus Klein
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
(attachment: SLA_Draft_Aquila_v3.pdf)
From: Claire Dawson <claire@aquila-health.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@aquila-health.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 10:18:00 -0500
Subject: Re: SLA uplift request and monthly credit cap

Thanks Markus — appreciate the options. A few follow-ups from our side:

- Finance will only accept a monthly cap equal to 100% of the monthly service fee (they will not agree to >1x). Can you confirm that Option A can commit to that?
- Compliance is willing to consider 99.97% for the pilot if there are stronger remedies for the 99.90–99.97 band (our concern is short, repeated blips). Can you expand the matrix so smaller degradations accrue credits faster?
- Maintenance: Aquila's infra team requires that scheduled maintenance that impacts production never exceeds 8 hours per quarter (not per month). Emergency maintenance is understood but should be limited in scope and communicated immediately.

I'll attach a one-page risk summary and our preferred redlines next.

Claire
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Claire Dawson <claire@aquila-health.com>, markus_klein@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA uplift request and monthly credit cap — proposed redline compromise

Claire / team —

Thanks — I took Markus' options and Aquila's asks and drafted a compromise we think is reasonable for a pilot while protecting both sides. Summary of proposed negotiated terms (redline summary attached: Aquila_SLA_redlines_20270310.docx):

1) Baseline availability: 99.97% monthly (applies for the initial 6-month pilot).
2) Remedy bands (monthly credit of monthly invoice):
   - >=99.97% — 0% credit
   - >=99.95% and <99.97% — 15% credit
   - >=99.90% and <99.95% — 40% credit
   - <99.90% — 100% credit
3) Monthly cap: capped at 100% of monthly invoice (per Aquila requirement).
4) Maintenance carveouts: scheduled maintenance will be limited to 8 hours per quarter (we accepted Aquila's ask), with a 7-day advance notification for non-emergency activities. Emergency maintenance is a carveout only if it meets the defined emergency criteria in section 5.4 (rare by design).
5) Repeated blips: we add a cumulative clause so that if there are more than 3 separate incidents in a 30-day window that each exceed 3 minutes, the remedy for the subsequent incidents increases by a multiplier (x1.5) to address repeated flapping.
6) EU/region parity: same terms apply in the US region for the pilot; regional differences negotiable at expansion.

We believe this preserves Aquila's financial cap request while giving stronger deterrents for repeated, short outages. If Aquila agrees we can circulate the redlined doc and route for signatures (DocuSign included).

Next steps: Claire, can you confirm the pilot scope (start date and monthly invoice baseline) so we can lock the cap calculation? If you prefer a call, Laura and I are free tomorrow 10–12 PT.

— Ben Carter
Director, Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
(attachment: Aquila_SLA_redlines_20270310.docx)
From: Claire Dawson <claire@aquila-health.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA uplift request and monthly credit cap — proposed redline compromise

Ben / Markus —

This looks good and addresses our main concerns. Quick confirmations:
- We accept 99.97% for the 6-month pilot with the bands you've proposed.
- Monthly cap 100% confirmed.
- Maintenance capped to 8 hours/quarter with 7-day notice — accepted.
- Please add the cumulative incident language to the final doc as drafted.

I'll send the pilot scope (expected start 2027-04-01; estimated monthly subscription $48,000) and then we can proceed with DocuSign. Please send the final redline and DocuSign envelope when ready.

Claire Dawson
Head of Procurement, Aquila Health
